title: Bounded preparation of a virtual-host configuration
statement: Let $P$ be a Boolean Turing machine with finitely many states and $P.k$ work tapes, let $j$ be a work-tape index of $P$, and let $m$ be a positive integer. There exist a finite-state Boolean Turing machine $D$, a state $e$ of $D$, injections from the $m$ tape indices and from the $1+P.k$ tape indices into the work tapes of $D$, a work-tape index $c$ outside the image of the latter injection, and a natural number $a$ such that the following holds. For every Boolean input word $y$ and Boolean words $x,u$, when $D$ starts on input $y$ with the encoding of $(x,u)$ on the tape indexed by the image of $0$ under the first injection and all other work tapes empty, there is a time $t\le a(|x|+|u|+1)$ at which its configuration has state $e$, input-head position $1$, and empty output. Its work tapes and head positions agree, under the second injection, with the virtual-host configuration whose simulated machine is in its initial state on input $x$, with $u$ on tape $j$, all other simulated work tapes empty, and boundary tag true; tape $c$ is empty with its head at position $0$, and the remaining tapes and head positions may be chosen arbitrarily. No earlier configuration in this run has state $e$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite-state Boolean Turing machine with $P.k$ work tapes
The bound and configuration property hold for every Boolean input word $y$ and Boolean words $x,u$
